nodes.one_liner: The reason-act loop vs. a single LLM call

nodes.title: How does tool calling actually work?
nodes.one_liner: Schemas, the model's tool request, and routing to code

nodes.title: Writing and wiring up your first tool
nodes.one_liner: Define a tool, expose it, execute the result

nodes.title: Building the agent loop
nodes.one_liner: Feeding tool results back until the task is done

outline.rationale: The user is a practitioner comfortable with plain LLM calls/prompting who wants to ship one working agent in their existing app. I skipped basics (prompting, model calls) and excluded multi-agent, eval, and framework comparison per their stated priorities. The outline follows the real dependency chain: first the conceptual shift (reason-act loop) that distinguishes an agent, then the core mechanic (tool calling), then hands-on tool implementation, then assembling the loop, then loop control/termination (which they specifically flagged), then robustness (error handling, a practical must for shipping), and finally integration into their app (their end goal). Nodes are MECE: concept, mechanism, build-a-tool, build-the-loop, stop-the-loop, harden-it, ship-it — each answers a distinct question with low overlap.
